title: DAT Green

No article body — signal is limited to the headline map of UK constitutional flashpoints.

insights.claim: Prospect runs a high-frequency legal column, 'The weekly constitutional', by a writer and lawyer who blogs on law and policy, with 153 articles listed on the author index.
insights.so_what: A high-cadence legal column is a usable early-warning feed for UK constitutional and administrative-law risk.

insights.claim: The page title renders as 'DAT Green' while the underlying author URL is for David Allen Green, indicating a scraping or CMS name-rendering discrepancy rather than a distinct author.
insights.so_what: Flags a metadata quality issue for anyone matching Prospect bylines programmatically.

themes.theme: UK constitutional flashpoints in the headline map

insights.claim: A listed headline asks whether the UK constitution can be safeguarded before the next general election, framing constitutional entrenchment as an urgent pre-election question rather than an academic one.
insights.so_what: Constitutional-safeguard debate ahead of a UK election is a governance-risk theme with read-through to policy stability and gilt-relevant institutional credibility.
insights.quote: Can we safeguard our constitution before the next general election?
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine

insights.claim: The listing shows a Burnham premiership being assessed as promising for constitutional reform, indicating the column treats the new leadership as a live constitutional-change opportunity.
insights.so_what: Constitutional reform under a Burnham government is a policy vector to watch for UK institutional and regulatory change.
insights.quote: A Burnham premiership looks promising for constitutional reform
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine

insights.claim: Recurring headline subjects — a Trump 'settlement' agreement defeated in court, the Palestine Action appeal and terrorism law, the end of the failed Rwanda asylum scheme, and modern ministers resigned to powerlessness — map the column's live docket of executive-power disputes.
insights.so_what: The recurring pattern is courts constraining executives on both sides of the Atlantic — a structural theme for policy-implementation risk.
insights.locator: Trump’s extraordinary ‘settlement’ agreement is defeated by the court
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine

insights.claim: The column argues modern ministers are resigned to powerlessness, an implied thesis that formal UK executive authority has been hollowed out relative to its appearance.
insights.so_what: If ministerial power is largely nominal, election outcomes matter less for policy delivery than the institutional machinery beneath them.
insights.quote: Modern ministers are resigned to powerlessness
